1	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
2	
3	/**
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
5	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
6	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
7	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
8	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
9	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
10	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
11	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
12	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
13	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
14	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
15	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
16	 * without a signature change here.
17	 *
18	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
19	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
20	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
21	 */
22	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
23	type CartToastFn = (options: { title: string; status: CartToastStatus }) => void;
24	
25	/**
26	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
27	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
28	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
29	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
30	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
31	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
32	 */
33	const getAddedToWishlistMessage = (productName: string): string => `${productName} added to Wishlist`;
34	const ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist';
35	const MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity';
36	
37	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
38	  /**
39	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
40	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
41	   * site. `success` status.
42	   */
43	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
44	  /**
45	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
46	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
47	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
48	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
49	   */
50	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
51	  /**
52	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
53	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
54	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
55	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
56	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
57	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
58	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
59	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
60	   * `error`").
61	   */
62	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
63	};
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
67	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
68	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
69	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
70	 * fires a toast.
71	 *
72	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
73	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
74	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
75	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
76	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
77	 * replaces.
78	 *
79	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
80	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
81	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
82	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
83	 */
84	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
85	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
86	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
87	  // this file actually depends on.
88	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
89	
90	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
91	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
92	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
93	    toast({ title, status });
94	  };
95	
96	  return {
97	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => emitCartMessage(getAddedToWishlistMessage(productName), 'success'),
98	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
99	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
100	  };
101	};
102
